Distinct from the question-bank MCQ **Drill** engine: Activities are authored content with their own answer keys, not timed runs over `qid` questions.\n\n## Language\n\n**Activity Centre**:\nThe module that hosts and lists Activities. The student\'s home for assigned skill work that isn\'t question-bank drilling.\n_Avoid_: Activities Centre, Skills Centre, Drill Centre\n\n**Activity**:\nOne bespoke skill exercise — a titled, self-contained set of authored items with an answer key, worked through with a coach (e.g. "Negation Station"). The unit a teacher assigns.\n_Avoid_: Skill drill, drill (reserved for the MCQ engine), station, module, game\n\n**Homepage**:\nJoshua-facing shorthand for an individual Activity\'s intro/start page: the page that shows the Activity title, item count, overview copy, example, and Start action before the student begins the first Question Set.\n_Avoid_: LSAT U landing page, Foyer, Activity Centre list\n\n**Question Set**:\nCodex-facing term for one complete per-question unit inside an Activity: the Question Type, the prompt, the response area, the coach feedback, the credited answer, and the answer key material used to judge the response. In the UI, this should still be labeled "Question N"; when Joshua says "question set," he means this full unit, not the collection of all questions.\n_Avoid_: Question collection, drill set, item bank\n\n**Question Type**:\nThe classification pill inside a Question Set that names what kind of statement or reasoning form the student is working with (e.g. "Universal Statement," "Conditional Statement," "Causal Statement"). This is the canonical term for the label currently shown above the prompt.\n_Avoid_: Category, tag, badge, label\n\n**Drill**:\nReserved term. The existing question-bank engine: a timed run over multiple-choice questions pulled by `qid`. An Activity is NOT a Drill.\n\n**Item**:\nOne prompt within an Activity that the student responds to (e.g. a single statement to negate). Ordered easy→hard as authored.\n_Avoid_: Question (overloaded with the qid question bank), problem, task\n\n**Credited answer**:\nThe author-supplied correct response to an Item, used as ground truth when the coach judges a student\'s response. Some Items carry several acceptable phrasings.\n_Avoid_: Solution, key answer, right answer\n\n**Coach**:\nThe conversational AI tutor that presents Items one at a time, reads the student\'s free-text response, and gives immediate supportive feedback against the credited answer. Built on the existing AI-gateway tutor pattern (`analyze-stem-response`).\n_Avoid_: Tutor (reserved for the standalone Tutor surface), bot, grader\n\n**Verdict**:\nThe coach\'s judgement of a single student response: `correct`, `partial`, or `incorrect`. `partial` captures a near-miss the Activity exists to teach (e.g. a polar-opposite instead of a true negation). Drives the assignment score and future weakness analytics.\n_Avoid_: Grade, mark, result\n\n**Activity assignment**:\nA per-student issued copy of an Activity, snapshotting its content at assign time and tracking the student\'s progress/score. Mirrors the homework `assignment` pattern; immutable snapshot once issued.\n_Avoid_: Homework (that\'s the MCQ-set pattern), task\n\n### Read, Recall, Colour\n\nThe four-step vocabulary of the RRC runner, plus the language its grading uses.\nThe source method\'s own words for these steps are listed under `_Avoid_` and are\nnever used in the product.\n\n**Chunk**:\nAn authored cut of a stimulus, roughly a sentence, carrying the Details that fall inside it. A guide for her eye and the unit content is written in, never a boundary she is held to: she reads, recalls and colours in whatever units she likes.\n_Avoid_: Line, segment, piece, part\n\n**Read** (step 1):\nThe silent reading of a chunk. Nothing is spoken.\n_Avoid_: Skim, study\n\n**Retelling** (step 2):\nSaying a chunk back out loud in her own words. **Retelling** is the word we use to each other and in code; the label a student reads is always **Tell it back**.\n_Avoid_: Reading Recall (its former name, which put "Recall" on two different steps), Say it back (the old student label), translate, translation, paraphrase, summary, repeat-back\n\n**Colouring In** (step 3):\nHer spoken reaction to the chunk she just recalled — a thought, doubt, example, or joke that fits that chunk and no other.\n_Avoid_: Quip, comment, annotation, reaction\n\n**The Recall** (step 4):\nThe end of a stimulus, worked with the text gone: she says the whole argument back from memory. Graded on Coverage.\n_Avoid_: Retelling (that is step 2), CLIR, recap, rebound, takeaway, The Read (see below: that is now the other number, not this step\'s former name)\n\n**The Read**:\nThe analytical takeaway, and the second graded number: what the argument is DOING, as opposed to what it says. Authored per stimulus as `the_read`, judged as two flags, `read_given` and `read_matches` ([ADR 0025](../../../docs/adr/0025-the-read-is-the-second-number.md)). It is a dimension of the grading, never a fifth step she is asked to perform out loud.\n\nIt was step 4\'s name until [ADR 0012](../../../docs/adr/0012-the-recall-is-a-recap-from-memory.md) renamed that step to The Recall, and this entry did not exist for the six days between 0012 and 0025, so "The Read" read as simply retired. It is not. On the Report Card, **Your Read** is correct and must not be collapsed into The Recall: they are the reasoning half and the memory half, and they fail differently.\n_Avoid_: Takeaway, the point, the gist, analysis\n\n**the move**:\nWhat a stimulus\'s Read turns on, in the judge\'s and the card\'s shorthand: the loophole, inference or conflict the argument runs on. Always defined on a surface before it is used, because "you found the move" means nothing to a student reading it for the first time.\n_Avoid_: The trick, the gotcha, the key (reserved for the authored answer)\n\n**Detail**:\nOne of the small authored facts a stimulus contains. PT102.S3.Q1 holds 21.\n_Avoid_: Point, fact, bullet, item (reserved for an Activity\'s prompt)\n\n**Coverage**:\nHow many of a stimulus\'s Details she carried, counted across everything she said about it rather than against any one Chunk.\n_Avoid_: Accuracy, completeness, recall rate\n\n**Reciting**:\nSaying a stimulus back close to word-for-word. A failure of the Retelling, not a step of its own: Coverage looks perfect and nothing was understood.\n_Avoid_: Parroting, copying, verbatim recall, memorising\n\n**Listing**:\nDelivering a stimulus as a flat run of facts rather than a story in her own words. The opposite failure to Reciting: Coverage looks perfect and the argument was never held together.\n_Avoid_: Shopping list, itemising, enumerating\n\n**Report Card**:\nWhat a finished section produces: every stimulus graded on its own merits, showing what she missed and what she got perfect, with her own recording playable beside it. Nothing here is a phase of the runner; these are things drawn on one\npage.\n\n**Section Launch**:\nThe page a student lands on before running an RRC section: the method as four Beats, her last few Attempts, and the one control that starts the run. `SectionLaunch` in code, `.sl-` in CSS. It replaces the editorial intro for section mode only; the eight typed Activities keep theirs.\n_Avoid_: The Chamber (the approved mockup\'s name for it, and already a world under `worlds/chamber/`), Homepage (that is an Activity\'s own intro page), intro, splash, lobby, dashboard\n\n**Beat**:\nInternal code term for one of the four method steps shown on Section Launch. Long\r\n * enough for a slow model call, short enough that nobody sits looking at a\r\n * spinner wondering whether the page is broken.\r\n */\r\nconst COACH_TIMEOUT_MS = 12_000;\r\n\r\nexport function useActivityCoach() {\r\n  const [judging, setJudging] = useState(false);\r\n\r\n  const judge = useCallback(async ({ item, studentResponse, attemptNo, coach, ideas }: JudgeArgs): Promise<JudgeResult> => {\r\n    setJudging(true);\r\n    // A hung gateway used to leave the textarea disabled and the spinner\r\n    // spinning with no way out: no timeout, no abort, nothing for the student\r\n    // to do but reload and lose the answer. The item now falls through to the\r\n    // Coach-unavailable path, which reveals the credited answer and records the\r\n    // attempt unjudged.\r\n    const abort = new AbortController();\r\n    const timeout = setTimeout(() => abort.abort(), COACH_TIMEOUT_MS);\r\n    try {\r\n      const { data, error } = await supabase.functions.invoke("activity-coach", {\r\n        signal: abort.signal,\r\n        body: {\r\n          statement: item.prompt,\r\n          studentResponse,\r\n          creditedAnswers: item.credited_answers,\r\n          explanation: item.explanation,\r\n          attemptNo,\r\n          coach,\r\n          category: item.category,\r\n          ideas,\r\n        },\r\n      });\r\n\r\n      if (error) {\r\n        const msg = error.message || "Coach unavailable";\r\n        console.error("[activity-coach] invoke failed", error);\r\n        return { ok: false, error: msg };\r\n      }\r\n      if (!data || typeof data.verdict !== "string") {\r\n        console.error("[activity-coach] malformed response", data);\r\n        return { ok: false, error: (data && data.error) || "Coach returned no verdict" };\r\n      }\r\n\r\n      // Coverage is only ever passed through, and only as an array of numbers.\r\n      // Anything else stays undefined so the checklist renders unjudged rather\r\n      // than claiming ticks nobody assigned.\r\n      const covered = Array.isArray(data.covered)\r\n        ? data.covered.filter((n: unknown) => typeof n === "number")\r\n        : undefined;\r\n\r\n      return { ok: true, verdict: { verdict: data.verdict, feedback: data.feedback ?? "", covered } };\r\n    } catch (e) {\r\n      if (abort.signal.aborted) {\r\n        console.error("[activity-coach] timed out", { ms: COACH_TIMEOUT_MS });\r\n        return { ok: false, error: "Coach timed out" };\r\n      }\r\n      console.error("[activity-coach] threw", e);\r\n      return { ok: false, error: e instanceof Error ? e.message : "Coach error" };\r\n    } finally {\r\n      clearTimeout(timeout);\r\n      setJudging(false);\r\n    }\r\n  }, []);\r\n\r\n  return { judge, judging };\r\n}\r\n\r\nimport { useEffect, useRef, useState } from "react";\r\nimport { toast } from "@/hooks/use-toast";\r\nimport { useActivityCoach } from "../hooks/useActivityCoach";\r\nimport type { ActivityCoach, ActivityItem, FeedbackState, ItemFormat, JudgeSource, Verdict } from "../api/types";\r\nimport { MAX_ATTEMPTS } from "../api/types";\r\nimport { clearDraft, saveDraft } from "../drafts";\r\nimport { StatementPanel } from "./StatementPanel";\r\nimport { ItemPrompt } from "./ItemPrompt";\r\n\r\ninterface ActivityItemViewProps {\r\n  item: ActivityItem;\r\n  format: ItemFormat;\r\n  isLast: boolean;\r\n  /** This Activity\'s judging brief, threaded through to the Coach. */\r\n  coach?: ActivityCoach;\r\n  /** Authored per Activity: what this drill asks the student to write. */\r\n  answerLabel?: string;\r\n  answerPlaceholder?: string;\r\n  /** Authored per Activity: what the credited answers after the first are called. */\r\n  creditedSecondaryLabel?: string;\r\n  /** True when the Activity\'s world already shows the prompt as written. */\r\n  promptInWorld?: boolean;\r\n  /**\r\n   * The world\'s local check for an answer the author already wrote down. When\r\n   * it returns true the item is correct, decided here, with no model call and\r\n   * no spinner. Absent for Activities whose answers have no authored structure,\r\n   * which then judge exactly as they did before.\r\n   */\r\n  fastPath?: (item: ActivityItem, response: string) => boolean;\r\n  /** The world\'s structural read of the answer, recorded as telemetry only. */\r\n  shadowFault?: (item: ActivityItem, response: string) => string | null;\r\n  /**\r\n   * Attempts already spent on this item in an earlier sitting, replayed from\r\n   * the attempt log. Zero for an item being met for the first time. The next\r\n   * submit continues the numbering rather than restarting it, so the student\r\n   * neither gets a spent attempt back nor writes a duplicate `attempt_no`.\r\n   */\r\n  initialAttempts?: number;\r\n  /** What they had written when they left, so a half-typed answer survives. */\r\n  initialValue?: string;\r\n  /**\r\n   * Where to cache what they are typing, before it is ever submitted. Until\r\n   * now text only reached storage as part of a submitted attempt, so closing\r\n   * the tab mid-sentence on question 24 lost the sentence.\r\n   */\r\n  draftKey?: string;\r\n  /** Fired once, when the item is resolved (correct, revealed, or coach failure). */\r\n  onResolved: (order: number, finalVerdict: Verdict | null) => void;\r\n  /** Append-only attempt record; best-effort, errors are toasted not thrown. */\r\n  onRecord: (args: {\r\n    itemOrder: number;\r\n    responseText: string;\r\n    verdict: Verdict | null;\r\n    attemptNo: number;\r\n    judgeSource?: JudgeSource;\r\n    shadowFault?: string | null;\r\n    latencyMs?: number;\r\n  }) => Promise<void>;\r\n  onNext: () => void;\r\n}\r\n\r\n/**\r\n * Per-item state machine: submit -> coach verdict -> (retry up to cap) ->\r\n * reveal credited answer -> next. Owns its own state; the runner remounts it\r\n * per item via a key so state resets cleanly.\r\n */\r\nexport function ActivityItemView({\r\n  item,\r\n  format,\r\n  isLast,\r\n  coach,\r\n  answerLabel,\r\n  answerPlaceholder,\r\n  creditedSecondaryLabel,\r\n  promptInWorld = false,\r\n  fastPath,\r\n  shadowFault,\r\n  initialAttempts = 0,\r\n  initialValue = "",\r\n  draftKey,\r\n  onResolved,\r\n  onRecord,\r\n  onNext,\r\n}: ActivityItemViewProps) {\r\n  const { judge, judging } = useActivityCoach();\r\n  const [value, setValue] = useState(initialValue);\r\n  const answerRef = useRef<HTMLTextAreaElement | null>(null);\r\n\r\n  // Debounced rather than per-keystroke: a draft is not durable state and does\r\n  // not deserve a write on every character.\r\n  useEffect(() => {\r\n    if (!draftKey) return;\r\n    const t = setTimeout(() => saveDraft(draftKey, value), 400);\r\n    return () => clearTimeout(t);\r\n  }, [draftKey, value]);\r\n  const [attempts, setAttempts] = useState(initialAttempts);\r\n  const [result, setResult] = useState<{ verdict: FeedbackState; feedback: string; covered?: number[] } | null>(null);\r\n  const [revealed, setRevealed] = useState(false);\r\n  const [resolved, setResolved] = useState(false);\r\n\r\n  const record = (args: Parameters<ActivityItemViewProps["onRecord"]>[0]) => {\r\n    // The attempt is the durable record now; the draft has done its job.\r\n    if (draftKey) clearDraft(draftKey);\r\n    void onRecord(args);\r\n  };\r\n\r\n  const resolve = (finalVerdict: Verdict | null, reveal: boolean) => {\r\n    setRevealed(reveal);\r\n    setResolved(true);\r\n    onResolved(item.order, finalVerdict);\r\n  };\r\n\r\n  const handleSubmit = async () => {\r\n    const attemptNo = attempts + 1;\r\n    const startedAt = performance.now();\r\n    const since = () => Math.round(performance.now() - startedAt);\r\n\r\n    // The author already wrote this answer down, so recognising it needs no\r\n    // model. Only an exact structural match against a credited answer takes\r\n    // this path, which is why it can be trusted: it confirms the answer key\r\n    // rather than reasoning about it. Everything else falls through and is\r\n    // judged exactly as before.\r\n    if (fastPath?.(item, value)) {\r\n      setAttempts(attemptNo);\r\n      setResult({ verdict: "correct", feedback: "" });\r\n      record({\r\n        itemOrder: item.order,\r\n        responseText: value,\r\n        verdict: "correct",\r\n        attemptNo,\r\n        judgeSource: "fast-path",\r\n        shadowFault: shadowFault?.(item, value) ?? null,\r\n        latencyMs: since(),\r\n      });\r\n      resolve("correct", false);\r\n      return;\r\n    }\r\n\r\n    const res = await judge({ item, studentResponse: value, attemptNo, coach });\r\n    setAttempts(attemptNo);\r\n\r\n    if (!res.ok || !res.verdict) {\r\n      // Coach failed. The student is never left stuck, so the credited answer is\r\n      // revealed and the item ends -- but it ends UNJUDGED. It used to end as\r\n      // "incorrect",…1591 tokens truncated…dition. Returning null is the honest\r\n  // answer: the world already falls back to the plain prompt and the authored\r\n  // answers, which is correct, rather than a diagram that is wrong.\r\n  if (/\\bif\\b|\\bthen\\b/i.test(ifText) || /\\bif\\b|\\bthen\\b/i.test(thenText)) return null;\r\n\r\n  return {\r\n    ifClause: { text: ifText, negated: isNegated(ifText) },\r\n    thenClause: { text: thenText, negated: isNegated(thenText) },\r\n  };\r\n}\r\n\r\n/**\r\n * The contrapositive as the machine performs it: the capsules swap tracks and\r\n * their polarity inverts, in one movement. This is derived rather than parsed\r\n * from the authored contrapositive, because the flip has to be a transformation\r\n * the student watches, not a second sentence that appears.\r\n */\r\nexport function flip(routing: Routing): Routing {\r\n  return {\r\n    ifClause: { text: routing.thenClause.text, negated: !routing.thenClause.negated },\r\n    thenClause: { text: routing.ifClause.text, negated: !routing.ifClause.negated },\r\n  };\r\n}\r\n\r\n/**\r\n * The indicator word the item turns on ("only if", "unless", "the only").\r\n * Authored as the first quoted span of the item\'s explanation, which is where\r\n * the bank puts it. Returned so the departures board can light it in place,\r\n * and only after the yard has routed.\r\n */\r\nexport function indicatorOf(explanation: string): string | undefined {\r\n  const m = explanation.match(/"([^"]{2,24})"/);\r\n  return m ? m[1] : undefined;\r\n}\r\n\r\n/* ------------------------------------------------------------------ *\r\n * Signal faults\r\n *\r\n * The locked partial set is three named errors, and the spec gives each one its\r\n * own choreography in the yard. Which one a student made is DERIVED here by\r\n * comparing their parsed routing against the credited one, rather than asked of\r\n * the Coach: the Coach returns a verdict and prose, and reading an error type\r\n * out of prose would be guessing. A structural comparison either finds the\r\n * error or honestly returns none.\r\n * ------------------------------------------------------------------ */\r\n\r\nexport type FaultKind = "reversal" | "dropped-negation" | "trimmed-condition";\r\nexport type FaultSide = "if" | "then";\r\n\r\nexport interface Fault {\r\n  kind: FaultKind;\r\n  /** Which track carries the affected capsule. Reversal affects both. */\r\n  side: FaultSide | "both";\r\n}\r\n\r\n// Words that carry polarity rather than content. Stripped before comparing, so\r\n// "is not refueled" still aligns with "is refueled" and the difference surfaces\r\n// as a dropped negation rather than as two unrelated clauses.\r\nconst POLARITY_TOKENS = new Set([\r\n  "not",\r\n  "no",\r\n  "never",\r\n  "cannot",\r\n  "cant",\r\n  "dont",\r\n  "doesnt",\r\n  "didnt",\r\n  "wont",\r\n  "wouldnt",\r\n  "isnt",\r\n  "arent",\r\n  "wasnt",\r\n  "werent",\r\n  "neither",\r\n  "nothing",\r\n]);\r\n\r\n// Function words carry no discriminating content for alignment.\r\nconst STOP_TOKENS = new Set(["a", "an", "the", "is", "are", "was", "were", "be", "been", "to", "of"]);\r\n\r\nfunction contentTokens(clause: string): string[] {\r\n  return clause\r\n    .toLowerCase()\r\n    .replace(/n\'t\\b/g, " not")\r\n    .replace(/[^a-z0-9\\s]/g, " ")\r\n    .split(/\\s+/)\r\n    .filter((t) => t && !POLARITY_TOKENS.has(t) && !STOP_TOKENS.has(t));\r\n}\r\n\r\n/** Share of the longer clause\'s content words the two clauses have in common. */\r\nfunction alignment(a: string, b: string): number {\r\n  const A = new Set(contentTokens(a));\r\n  const B = new Set(contentTokens(b));\r\n  if (!A.size || !B.size) return 0;\r\n  let shared = 0;\r\n  for (const t of A) if (B.has(t)) shared += 1;\r\n  return shared / Math.max(A.size, B.size);\r\n}\r\n\r\n/** True when `short` says a strict subset of what `full` says, and materially less. */\r\nfunction isTrimmed(short: string, full: string): boolean {\r\n  const S = contentTokens(short);\r\n  const F = new Set(contentTokens(full));\r\n  if (S.length < 2 || !S.every((t) => F.has(t))) return false;\r\n  return F.size - new Set(S).size >= 2;\r\n}\r\n\r\n/**\r\n * Name the student\'s error, or return null when their routing is credited-clean\r\n * or too far from it to classify. Null is a real answer: the yard then makes no\r\n * claim about which mistake was made and the Coach takes the item.\r\n */\r\nexport function diagnose(credited: Routing, student: Routing | null): Fault | null {\r\n  if (!student) return null;\r\n\r\n  const straight =\r\n    alignment(student.ifClause.text, credited.ifClause.text) +\r\n    alignment(student.thenClause.text, credited.thenClause.text);\r\n  const crossed =\r\n    alignment(student.ifClause.text, credited.thenClause.text) +\r\n    alignment(student.thenClause.text, credited.ifClause.text);\r\n\r\n  // Both clauses sit on the wrong track: the reversal, the error this drill\r\n  // exists to kill. Requires a real crossed match, not merely a weak straight one.\r\n  if (crossed > straight && crossed >= 1) return { kind: "reversal", side: "both" };\r\n  if (straight < 1) return null;\r\n\r\n  // Routed correctly. Anything left is a fault inside a capsule.\r\n  if (student.ifClause.negated !== credited.ifClause.negated) {\r\n    return { kind: "dropped-negation", side: "if" };\r\n  }\r\n  if (student.thenClause.negated !== credited.thenClause.negated) {\r\n    return { kind: "dropped-negation", side: "then" };\r\n  }\r\n  if (isTrimmed(student.ifClause.text, credited.ifClause.text)) {\r\n    return { kind: "trimmed-condition", side: "if" };\r\n  }\r\n  if (isTrimmed(student.thenClause.text, credited.thenClause.text)) {\r\n    return { kind: "trimmed-condition", side: "then" };\r\n  }\r\n  return null;\r\n}\r\n\r\n/** Whether the student\'s routing differs enough from credited to be worth showing. */\r\nexport function differs(credited: Routing, student: Routing | null): boolean {\r\n  if (!student) return false;\r\n  const same = (a: Clause, b: Clause) =>\r\n    a.negated === b.negated && contentTokens(a.text).join(" ") === contentTokens(b.text).join(" ");\r\n  return !(same(student.ifClause, credited.ifClause) && same(student.thenClause, credited.thenClause));\r\n}\r\n\r\n/* ------------------------------------------------------------------ *\r\n * The fast path\r\n *\r\n * A student who writes an answer the author already wrote down needs no model\r\n * to confirm it. This recognises exactly that case and nothing else.\r\n *\r\n * It compares against EVERY credited answer, not just the first. In this bank\r\n * the second credited answer is the contrapositive, and on items 46, 47 and 48\r\n * it is a genuinely different logical direction. Checking only slot 0 would\r\n * grade the answer the task explicitly asks for as wrong.\r\n *\r\n * It makes no inference: a correct paraphrase the author did not write ("fans\r\n * are running all night" for "fans run overnight") falls through, because\r\n * `differs` compares token sequences with no stemming or synonyms. Falling\r\n * through means asking the Coach, which is the safe direction to fail in.\r\n * ------------------------------------------------------------------ */\r\n\r\n/** Bumped whenever the rules above change, so shadow telemetry is attributable. */\r\nexport const PARSER_VERSION = "routing-1";\r\n\r\n/**\r\n * True when the student\'s routing is structurally identical to one of the\r\n * item\'s credited answers. False is not a claim that the answer is wrong; it\r\n * only means this cannot be settled without the Coach.\r\n */\r\nexport function matchesAnyCredited(creditedAnswers: string[] | undefined, response: string): boolean {\r\n  const student = parseRouting(response);\r\n  if (!student) return false;\r\n  return (creditedAnswers ?? []).some((credited) => {\r\n    const routing = parseRouting(credited);\r\n    return routing ? !differs(routing, student) : false;\r\n  });\r\n}\r\n\r\n/* ------------------------------------------------------------------ *\r\n * The flip, and where it is safe to perform\r\n *\r\n * `flip()` swaps the clauses and inverts the polarity flag, but it cannot\r\n * rewrite the clause TEXT -- so a flipped rail used to read "the beacon goes\r\n * dark" with the lamp lit, directly above a plate reading "If the beacon did\r\n * not go dark". They contradicted each other on screen, in the drill about\r\n * negation. That is why the flip was never performed.\r\n *\r\n * Making it true means showing polarity as readable text rather than as an\r\n * unlabelled lamp, which needs the clause split into a positive core and a\r\n * polarity. That split is only sound for some of the bank:\r\n *\r\n *   - "the string quartet is not"      an ellipsis; the core is a noun phrase\r\n *   - "lack impulsive onsets"          lexical negation, invisible to the list\r\n *   - "no fixture is shielded"         the bare no + noun path\r\n *   - "both X and Y" / "X rather than Y"   NOT [...] does not resolve the scope\r\n *\r\n * Rather than guess at those, an item earns the animated flip only by passing a\r\n * gate that is checkable in a test. Everything else shows the AUTHORED\r\n * contrapositive plate with a static junction and no derived rails, which is\r\n * not a downgrade: the authored sentence is correct by construction.\r\n * ------------------------------------------------------------------ */\r\n\r\n/**\r\n * Negations that behave as auxiliaries: they sit between a subject and its\r\n * predicate, and swapping them for their positive form leaves a clause that\r\n * still reads. Longest-first so "cannot" is never matched as "can not".\r\n */\r\nconst POLARITY_PAIRS: [negative: string, positive: string][] = [\r\n  ["cannot", "can"],\r\n  ["can not", "can"],\r\n  ["does not", "does"],\r\n  ["do not", "do"],\r\n  ["did not", "did"],\r\n  ["is not", "is"],\r\n  ["are not", "are"],\r\n  ["was not", "was"],\r\n  ["were not", "were"],\r\n  ["will not", "will"],\r\n  ["would not", "would"],\r\n  ["has not", "has"],\r\n  ["have not", "have"],\r\n  ["had not", "had"],\r\n  ["may not", "may"],\r\n  ["must not", "must"],\r\n];\r\n\r\n/**\r\n * Negation the list above cannot lift: it is carried by the verb itself, by a\r\n * determiner, or by a word with no positive twin. A clause containing any of\r\n * these is negative in a way this module cannot state positively, so it is\r\n * excluded rather than guessed at.\r\n */\r\nconst UNLIFTABLE_NEGATION =\r\n  /\\b(never|neither|nothing|none|nobody|nor|without|lack|lacks|lacked|lacking|absent|fail|fails|failed|unable|refuses?|refused|omits?|omitted|missing|no longer|barred|prevents?|prevented)\\b/i;\r\n\r\n/** Structures where a single polarity token cannot say what it applies to. */\r\nconst NEEDS_SCOPE = /\\b(and|or|but|rather than|instead of|both|either|unless|except)\\b|[;:]/i;\r\n\r\nexport interface Polarity {\r\n  /** The clause stated positively, ready to carry a polarity token beside it. */\r\n  core: string;\r\n  /** Whether the clause as authored is negative. */\r\n  negated: boolean;\r\n}\r\n\r\n/**\r\n * Split a clause into a positive core and a polarity, or return null when that\r\n * cannot be done truthfully. Null is the load-bearing return: it is what keeps\r\n * an unsound flip off the screen.\r\n */\r\nexport function readPolarity(clause: string): Polarity | null {\r\n  const text = clause.trim();\r\n  if (!text) return null;\r\n  if (NEEDS_SCOPE.test(text)) return null;\r\n  if (UNLIFTABLE_NEGATION.test(text)) return null;\r\n  // The bare "no + noun" path: negation carried by a determiner, which cannot be\r\n  // lifted out without rewriting the noun phrase.\r\n  if (/\\bno\\s+\\w/i.test(text)) return null;\r\n\r\n  const lower = text.toLowerCase();\r\n  const hits = POLARITY_PAIRS.filter(([negative]) =>\r\n    new RegExp(`\\\\b${negative.replace(/ /g, "\\\\s+")}\\\\b`, "i").test(lower),\r\n  );\r\n  if (hits.length === 0) {\r\n    // No negation signal of any kind. Guard against the contracted forms the\r\n    // pair list does not carry rather than calling the clause positive.\r\n    if (/n\'t\\b/i.test(text)) return null;\r\n    return { core: text, negated: false };\r\n  }\r\n  if (hits.length > 1) return null; // two negations: not this module\'s problem\r\n\r\n  const [negative, positive] = hits[0];\r\n  const span = new RegExp(`\\\\b${negative.replace(/ /g, "\\\\s+")}\\\\b`, "i");\r\n  // An ellipsis ends ON the negation ("the string quartet is not"), so lifting\r\n  // it leaves a noun phrase rather than a clause.\r\n  if (span.test(text) && /\\b(is|are|was|were|does|do|did|has|have|had|will|would|may|must|can)?\\s*not\\s*$/i.test(text)) {\r\n    return null;\r\n  }\r\n  const core = text.replace(span, positive).replace(/\\s+/g, " ").trim();\r\n  if (!core || core === text) return null;\r\n  return { core, negated: true };\r\n}\r\n\r\n/** A routing whose every clause can be stated positively with a polarity beside it. */\r\nexport interface DerivedRouting {\r\n  ifClause: Polarity;\r\n  thenClause: Polarity;\r\n}\r\n\r\n/**\r\n * The contrapositive as readable structure: the clauses swap tracks and each\r\n * polarity inverts, with the core text carried across untouched. Returns null\r\n * when either clause cannot be read, which is the signal to show the authored\r\n * plate instead of a derived diagram.\r\n */\r\nexport function derivedFlip(routing: Routing): DerivedRouting | null {\r\n  const ifSide = readPolarity(routing.ifClause.text);\r\n  const thenSide = readPolarity(routing.thenClause.text);\r\n  if (!ifSide || !thenSide) return null;\r\n  return {\r\n    ifClause: { core: thenSide.core, negated: !thenSide.negated },\r\n    thenClause: { core: ifSide.core, negated: !ifSide.negated },\r\n  };\r\n}\r\n\r\n// Authored contrapositives are written loosely: only 13 of 62 use "If X, then\r\n// Y", while 36 drop the "then". This reads that looser form, and is used ONLY\r\n// to check a derived flip against what the author wrote. It never feeds the\r\n// display, which still requires the strict form.\r\nconst IF_COMMA = /^\\s*if\\s+(.+?),\\s*(.+?)\\s*$/i;\r\n\r\nexport function parseAuthoredContrapositive(answer: string): Routing | null {\r\n  const strict = parseRouting(answer);\r\n  if (strict) return strict;\r\n\r\n  const match = trimTerminal(answer).match(IF_COMMA);\r\n  if (!match) return null;\r\n  const ifText = trimTerminal(match[1]);\r\n  const thenText = trimTerminal(match[2]);\r\n  if (!ifText || !thenText) return null;\r\n  if (/\\bif\\b|\\bthen\\b/i.test(ifText) || /\\bif\\b|\\bthen\\b/i.test(thenText)) return null;\r\n  return {\r\n    ifClause: { text: ifText, negated: isNegated(ifText) },\r\n    thenClause: { text: thenText, negated: isNegated(thenText) },\r\n  };\r\n}\r\n\r\n/**\r\n * Whether this item earns the animated flip.\r\n *\r\n * The last condition is the one that makes the rest trustworthy: the derived\r\n * polarity must AGREE with the polarity of the sentence the author wrote. That\r\n * is not belt and braces. Items 52 and 53 turn on "takes the color unevenly" --\r\n * lexical negation carried by a prefix, invisible to any list of negation words\r\n * worth maintaining -- and the derived flip would have rendered a double\r\n * negative the student had to untangle. ## assistant

The ranked causes are:

1. `matchesAnyCredited` requires nearly identical clause tokens, so valid paraphrases fall through.
2. `ActivityItemView` has no authoritative local-verdict path. Its only local answer is “exactly correct”; every other answer invokes AI.
3. The existing structural fault detector already recognizes direction and negation, but it is telemetry-only.
4. One two-rule item needs an explicit deterministic fallback because the single-rule parser intentionally rejects it.

I’m proceeding with #1 through #3 as the main cause. The regression test will require the live paraphrase case to receive a local verdict without invoking the Coach.

Ordered longest-first so\r\n// "cannot" is not matched by "not" with a different span.\r\nconst NEGATIONS = [\r\n  "cannot",\r\n  "can not",\r\n  "does not",\r\n  "did not",\r\n  "do not",\r\n  "will not",\r\n  "would not",\r\n  "is not",\r\n  "are not",\r\n  "was not",\r\n  "were not",\r\n  "may not",\r\n  "must not",\r\n  "no longer",\r\n  "not ",\r\n  "n\'t",\r\n  "never",\r\n  "neither",\r\n  "nothing",\r\n];\r\n\r\n/** Whether a clause reads as negative, which lights the capsule\'s polarity ring. */\r\nexport function isNegated(clause: string): boolean {\r\n  const s = ` ${clause.toLowerCase().trim()} `;\r\n  if (/\\bno\\s+\\w/.test(s) && !/\\bno\\s+longer\\b/.test(s)) return true;\r\n  return NEGATIONS.some((n) => s.includes(n));\r\n}\r\n\r\nfunction trimTerminal(s: string): string {\r\n  return s.replace(/\\s*[.;]\\s*$/, "").trim();\r\n}\r\n\r\n/**\r\n * Parse an authored "If X, then Y." credited answer into its two clauses.\r\n * Returns null when the answer is not in that form, which the world treats as\r\n * "no routing available" and falls back to plain text rather than guessing.\r\n */\r\nexport function parseRouting(creditedAnswer: string): Routing | null {\r\n  const match = trimTerminal(creditedAnswer).match(IF_THEN);\r\n  if (!match) return null;\r\n\r\n  const [, sufficient, necessary] = match;\r\n  const ifText = trimTerminal(sufficient);\r\n  const thenText = trimTerminal(necessary);\r\n  if (!ifText || !thenText) return null;\r\n\r\n  // A sentence carrying TWO conditionals is not two clauses, and the regex above\r\n  // will happily hand back the whole tail as one. Exact authored wording is\n+  // still deterministically knowable even though the one-routing visual parser\n+  // correctly refuses to squeeze two rules onto one pair of tracks.\n+  if (answers.some((answer) => normalizedSentence(answer) === normalized)) {\n+    return { verdict: \"correct\", feedback: \"\" };\n+  }\n+\n+  const student = parseRouting(response);\n+  if (!student) {\n+    return {\n+      verdict: \"incorrect\",\n+      feedback: \"Use one complete structure: If [sufficient], then [necessary].\",\n+    };\n+  }\n+\n+  const candidates = answers.map(parseRouting).filter((routing): routing is Routing => Boolean(routing));\n+\n+  for (const credited of candidates) {\n+    const sameContent = aligned(student.ifClause, credited.ifClause) && aligned(student.thenClause, credited.thenClause);\n+    if (\n+      sameContent &&\n+      samePolarity(student.ifClause, credited.ifClause) &&\n+      samePolarity(student.thenClause, credited.thenClause) &&\n+      !isTrimmed(student.ifClause.text, credited.ifClause.text) &&\n+      !isTrimmed(student.thenClause.text, credited.thenClause.text)\n+    ) {\n+      return { verdict: \"correct\", feedback: \"\" };\n+    }\n+  }\n+\n+  for (const credited of candidates) {\n+    const straight = aligned(student.ifClause, credited.ifClause) && aligned(student.thenClause, credited.thenClause);\n+    if (straight && (!samePolarity(student.ifClause, credited.ifClause) || !samePolarity(student.thenClause, credited.thenClause))) {\n+      return {\n+        verdict: \"partial\",\n+        feedback: \"Your clauses are on the right tracks, but a negation changed. Check every not, no, never, and cannot.\",\n+      };\n+    }\n+  }\n+\n+  for (const credited of candidates) {\n+    const reversed = aligned(student.ifClause, credited.thenClause) && aligned(student.thenClause, credited.ifClause);\n+    if (reversed) {\n+      return {\n+        verdict: \"partial\",\n+        feedback: \"You reversed the arrow. The necessary condition does not guarantee the sufficient condition.\",\n+      };\n+    }\n+  }\n+\n+  for (const credited of candidates) {\n+    if (isTrimmed(student.ifClause.text, credited.ifClause.text) || isTrimmed(student.thenClause.text, credited.thenClause.text)) {\n+      return {\n+        verdict: \"partial\",\n+        feedback: \"One side of the conditional lost part of the original condition. Carry the whole condition across.\",\n+      };\n+    }\n+  }\n+\n+  return {\n+    verdict: \"incorrect\",\n+    feedback: \"The direction or content does not match the statement. Find the trigger, then identify what it requires.\",\n+  };\n+}\n*** End Patch";

Below md the card starts where the band\r\n       ends. */\r\n    <div className="flex items-start px-5 py-6 md:min-h-screen md:items-center md:px-12 md:py-12">\r\n      <section\r\n        key={activeItem.order}\r\n        aria-current="step"\r\n        className="ac-question-card w-full"\r\n      >\r\n        <div className="text-[11px] font-bold uppercase tracking-[0.18em] text-[hsl(var(--aw-eyebrow,var(--ac-emerald-strong)))]">\r\n          Question {activeIndex + 1}\r\n        </div>\r\n\r\n        <div className="mt-4">\r\n          <ActivityItemView\r\n            key={activeItem.order}\r\n            item={activeItem}\r\n            format={format}\r\n            coach={coach}\r\n            answerLabel={answerLabel}\r\n            answerPlaceholder={answerPlaceholder}\r\n            creditedSecondaryLabel={creditedSecondaryLabel}\r\n            promptInWorld={promptInWorld}\r\n            fastPath={fastPath}\r\n            shadowFault={shadowFault}\r\n            initialAttempts={resumeAttempts}\r\n            initialValue={resumeValue}\r\n            draftKey={draftKeyFor?.(activeItem.order)}\r\n            isLast={activeIndex === items.length - 1}\r\n            onResolved={onResolved}\r\n            onRecord={onRecord}\r\n            onNext={onNext}\r\n          />\r\n        </div>\r\n      </section>\r\n    </div>\r\n  );\r\n}\r\n\r\n'}]

token;\r\n  if (aliased.length > 5 && aliased.endsWith("ing")) {\r\n    const root = aliased.slice(0, -3);\r\n    return root.length > 2 && root.at(-1) === root.at(-2) ? root.slice(0, -1) : root;\r\n  }\r\n  if (aliased.length > 4 && aliased.endsWith("ies")) return `${aliased.slice(0, -3)}y`;\r\n  if (aliased.length > 4 && aliased.endsWith("ed")) return aliased.slice(0, -2);\r\n  if (aliased.length > 3 && aliased.endsWith("s") && !aliased.endsWith("ss")) return aliased.slice(0, -1);\r\n  return aliased;\r\n}\r\n\r\nfunction contentTokens(clause: string): string[] {\r\n  return clause\r\n    .toLowerCase()\r\n    .replace(/n\'t\\b/g, " not")\r\n    .replace(/[^a-z0-9\\s]/g, " ")\r\n    .split(/\\s+/)\r\n    .filter((t) => t && !POLARITY_TOKENS.has(t) && !STOP_TOKENS.has(t))\r\n    .map(stem);\r\n}\r\n\r\n/** Share of the longer clause\'s content words the two clauses have in common. */\r\nfunction alignment(a: string, b: string): number {\r\n  const A = new Set(contentTokens(a));\r\n  const B = new Set(contentTokens(b));\r\n  if (!A.size || !B.size) return 0;\r\n  let shared = 0;\r\n  for (const t of A) if (B.has(t)) shared += 1;\r\n  return shared / Math.max(A.size, B.size);\r\n}\r\n\r\n/** True when `short` says a strict subset of what `full` says, and materially less. */\r\nfunction isTrimmed(short: string, full: string): boolean {\r\n  const S = contentTokens(short);\r\n  const F = new Set(contentTokens(full));\r\n  if (S.length < 2 || !S.every((t) => F.has(t))) return false;\r\n  return F.size - new Set(S).size >= 2;\r\n}\r\n\r\n/**\r\n * Name the student\'s error, or return null when their routing is credited-clean\r\n * or too far from it to classify. Requires a real crossed match, not merely a weak straight one.\r\n  if (crossed > straight && crossed >= 1) return { kind: "reversal", side: "both" };\r\n  if (straight < 1) return null;\r\n\r\n  // Routed correctly. In this bank\r\n * the second credited answer is the contrapositive, and on items 46, 47 and 48\r\n * it is a genuinely different logical direction. Checking only slot 0 would\r\n * grade the answer the task explicitly asks for as wrong.\r\n *\r\n * It makes no inference: a correct paraphrase the author did not write ("fans\r\n * are running all night" for "fans run overnight") falls through, because\r\n * `differs` compares token sequences with no stemming or synonyms. Falling\r\n * through means asking the Coach, which is the safe direction to fail in.\r\n * ------------------------------------------------------------------ */\r\n\r\n/** Bumped whenever the rules above change, so shadow telemetry is attributable. */\r\nexport const PARSER_VERSION = "routing-2-local-judge";\r\n\r\n/**\r\n * True when the student\'s routing is structurally identical to one of the\r\n * item\'s credited answers. False is not a claim that the answer is wrong; it\r\n * only means this cannot be settled without the Coach.\r\n */\r\nexport function matchesAnyCredited(creditedAnswers: string[] | undefined, response: string): boolean {\r\n  const student = parseRouting(response);\r\n  if (!student) return false;\r\n  return (creditedAnswers ?? []).some((credited) => {\r\n    const routing = parseRouting(credited);\r\n    return routing ? !differs(routing, student) : false;\r\n  });\r\n}\r\n\r\nexport interface LocalConditionalVerdict {\r\n  verdict: "correct" | "partial" | "incorrect";\r\n  feedback: string;\r\n}\r\n\r\n# Activity Centre\r\n\r\nThe home for bespoke, coach-led skill exercises (e.g. Negation Station) that a student is assigned and works through conversationally. Distinct from the question-bank MCQ **Drill** engine: Activities are authored content with their own answer keys, not timed runs over `qid` questions.\r\n\r\n## Language\r\n\r\n**Activity Centre**:\r\nThe module that hosts and lists Activities. The student\'s home for assigned skill work that isn\'t question-bank drilling.\r\n_Avoid_: Activities Centre, Skills Centre, Drill Centre\r\n\r\n**Activity**:\r\nOne bespoke skill exercise — a titled, self-contained set of authored items with an answer key, worked through with a coach (e.g. "Negation Station"). The unit a teacher assigns.\r\n_Avoid_: Skill drill, drill (reserved for the MCQ engine), station, module, game\r\n\r\n**Homepage**:\r\nJoshua-facing shorthand for an individual Activity\'s intro/start page: the page that shows the Activity title, item count, overview copy, example, and Start action before the student begins the first Question Set.\r\n_Avoid_: LSAT U landing page, Foyer, Activity Centre list\r\n\r\n**Question Set**:\r\nCodex-facing term for one complete per-question unit inside an Activity: the Question Type, the prompt, the response area, the coach feedback, the credited answer, and the answer key material used to judge the response. In the UI, this should still be labeled "Question N"; when Joshua says "question set," he means this full unit, not the collection of all questions.\r\n_Avoid_: Question collection, drill set, item bank\r\n\r\n**Question Type**:\r\nThe classification pill inside a Question Set that names what kind of statement or reasoning form the student is working with (e.g. "Universal Statement," "Conditional Statement," "Causal Statement"). This is the canonical term for the label currently shown above the prompt.\r\n_Avoid_: Category, tag, badge, label\r\n\r\n**Drill**:\r\nReserved term. The existing question-bank engine: a timed run over multiple-choice questions pulled by `qid`. An Activity is NOT a Drill.\r\n\r\n**Item**:\r\nOne prompt within an Activity that the student responds to (e.g. a single statement to negate). Ordered easy→hard as authored.\r\n_Avoid_: Question (overloaded with the qid question bank), problem, task\r\n\r\n**Credited answer**:\r\nThe author-supplied correct response to an Item, used as ground truth when the coach judges a student\'s response. Some Items carry several acceptable phrasings.\r\n_Avoid_: Solution, key answer, right answer\r\n\r\n**Coach**:\r\nThe conversational AI tutor that presents Items one at a time, reads the student\'s free-text response, and gives immediate supportive feedback against the credited answer. Built on the existing AI-gateway tutor pattern (`analyze-stem-response`).\r\n_Avoid_: Tutor (reserved for the standalone Tutor surface), bot, grader\r\n\r\n**Verdict**:\r\nThe coach\'s judgement of a single student response: `correct`, `partial`, or `incorrect`. `partial` captures a near-miss the Activity exists to teach (e.g. a polar-opposite instead of a true negation). Drives the assignment score and future weakness analytics.\r\n_Avoid_: Grade, mark, result\r\n\r\n**Activity assignment**:\r\nA per-student issued copy of an Activity, snapshotting its content at assign time and tracking the student\'s progress/score. Mirrors the homework `assignment` pattern; immutable snapshot once issued.\r\n_Avoid_: Homework (that\'s the MCQ-set pattern), task\r\n\r\n### Read, Recall, Colour\r\n\r\nThe four-step vocabulary of the RRC runner, plus the language its grading uses.\r\nThe source method\'s own words for these steps are listed under `_Avoid_` and are\r\nnever used in the product.\r\n\r\n**Chunk**:\r\nAn authored cut of a stimulus, roughly a sentence, carrying the Details that fall inside it. A guide for her eye and the unit content is written in, never a boundary she is held to: she reads, recalls and colours in whatever units she likes.\r\n_Avoid_: Line, segment, piece, part\r\n\r\n**Read** (step 1):\r\nThe silent reading of a chunk. Nothing is spoken.\r\n_Avoid_: Skim, study\r\n\r\n**Retelling** (step 2):\r\nSaying a chunk back out loud in her own words. **Retelling** is the word we use to each other and in code; the label a student reads is always **Tell it back**.\r\n'}]
